request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "Instructions were missed.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "target": "global",
    "text": "Always carefully follow instructions and do high quality work."
  },
  "remedy_type": "claude-md",
  "routing_rationale": "A rule may help."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":1,"justification":"The text prescribes no concrete behavior change (no specific check, format, or step to follow), so it cannot alter what the agent actually does differently next time."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":1,"justification":"\"Always carefully follow instructions and do high quality work\" is a pure platitude with no scope or mechanism, sitting at the vague end with no generalizable rule content."},"trigger_quality":{"score":1,"justification":"There is no 'Use when ...' condition or any situational trigger at all — it's phrased as a blanket always-on statement, which is inappropriate even for a claude-md rule since it gives no signal for when it's load-bearing."},"leakage":{"score":5,"justification":"The remedy text contains no project-specific nouns, file names, or evidence details, so there is no leakage risk, albeit only because it says nothing substantive."},"routing_fitness":{"score":1,"justification":"The failure_statement is too vague to justify any remedy, and adding a permanent, unconditional global CLAUDE.md line for an unspecified 'instructions were missed' incident is the wrong (and non-cheapest-adequate) tool — it adds standing noise to every future session without addressing a diagnosed cause."}}

actionability.justification: The text prescribes no concrete behavior change (no specific check, format, or step to follow), so it cannot alter what the agent actually does differently next time.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: "Always carefully follow instructions and do high quality work" is a pure platitude with no scope or mechanism, sitting at the vague end with no generalizable rule content.

leakage.justification: The remedy text contains no project-specific nouns, file names, or evidence details, so there is no leakage risk, albeit only because it says nothing substantive.

routing_fitness.justification: The failure_statement is too vague to justify any remedy, and adding a permanent, unconditional global CLAUDE.md line for an unspecified 'instructions were missed' incident is the wrong (and non-cheapest-adequate) tool — it adds standing noise to every future session without addressing a diagnosed cause.

trigger_quality.justification: There is no 'Use when ...' condition or any situational trigger at all — it's phrased as a blanket always-on statement, which is inappropriate even for a claude-md rule since it gives no signal for when it's load-bearing.
